reforms.description: The Canadian government improved the targeting of business R&D support by adjusting the SR&ED tax subsidies and increasing direct grants for business innovation, with nearly CAD1.9 billion allocated over four years.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased funding for R&D is expected to enhance innovation and productivity in the private sector.
reforms.status_evidence: The reform has been put into effect as of 2014.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant change in the allocation of public funds for business R&D.
reforms.source_quote: Budget 2012 announced changes to simplify, enhance predictability and improve the cost-effectiveness of the SR&ED programme (with all changes fully in effect in 2014).

reforms.description: The Venture Capital Action Plan (VCAP) was announced to deploy CAD400 million in new capital to strengthen Canada's venture capital industry and increase risk financing for innovative firms.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By increasing risk financing, the VCAP aims to enhance the capacity of innovative firms to grow and succeed.
reforms.status_evidence: The VCAP has been successfully implemented since its announcement.
reforms.importance_rationale: This plan represents a major initiative to bolster the venture capital landscape in Canada.
reforms.source_quote: The Government of Canada announced in January 2013 the Venture Capital Action Plan (VCAP), a comprehensive strategy for deploying CAD400 million in new capital.

reforms.description: The Business Innovation Access Program was launched to connect small and medium-sized enterprises with research institutions to facilitate the commercialization of ideas and products.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Facilitating connections between SMEs and research institutions is expected to enhance innovation and commercialization efforts.
reforms.status_evidence: The program has been launched and is operational.
reforms.importance_rationale: While significant, this program is not as transformative as the major reforms.
reforms.source_quote: In March 2014, the federal government launched the Business Innovation Access Program, to connect small and medium-sized enterprises with universities, colleges and other research institutions.

reforms.description: The new Canada Job Grant aims to align public training expenditures with labor market demand by allowing employers to participate in training decisions, ensuring better job matching.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By aligning training with labor market needs, the initiative is expected to enhance workforce skills and employability.
reforms.status_evidence: The grant has been implemented and is operational.
reforms.importance_rationale: This initiative represents a significant shift in how public training funds are allocated and utilized.
reforms.source_quote: The new Canada Job Grant is intended to orient public training expenditures towards meeting labour market demand, which would improve job matching.

reforms.description: The Canada Apprentice Loan was proposed to provide interest-free loans of up to CAD 4000 for apprentices during their technical training, aimed at reducing financial barriers to completing in-school training.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By reducing financial barriers, the loan is expected to encourage more individuals to complete their technical training.
reforms.status_evidence: The proposal has been announced but not yet implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: While beneficial, this proposal is not as significant as major reforms.
reforms.source_quote: To reduce the financial barrier to apprentices completing their in-school training, the interest-free Canada Apprentice Loan of up to CAD 4000 per period of technical training for apprentices in their first Red Seal trade was proposed in the 2014 federal budget.

reforms.description: The federal government proposed to work with provinces to harmonize apprenticeship programs across all provinces and territories to facilitate inter-provincial mobility and reduce barriers to completion.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Harmonizing apprenticeship programs is expected to improve access and completion rates for apprentices across Canada.
reforms.status_evidence: The proposal has been announced but not yet implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: This proposal is significant but not as transformative as major reforms.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government should continue to work with provinces to harmonise programmes.
